1THE AL-HAMD ISLAMIC UNIVERSITY, QUETTA ACT, 2005
 
(Balochistan Act II of 2005)
[20th April, 2005]

An Act for the establishment of Al-Hamd Islamic 
University at Quetta.

Preamble. 
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the 
establishment of the  Al-Hamd Islamic University and for 
matters connected therewith;
It is hereby enacted as follows:—

Short title and 
Commencement.

1.
(1)
This Act may be called the Al-Hamd Islamic 
University, Quetta Act, 2005.

(2)
It shall come into force at once.

Definitions.
2.
In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,—

(1)
“Academic Council” means the Academic
Council of the University;

(2)
“Authority” means any of the Authorities of the
University specified in section 7;

(3)
“Board” means the Board of Governors of the
University;

1

Balochistan Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 28, dated 20th April, 2005.

(4)
“Chancellor” means the Chancellor of the
University;

(5)
“Faculty” means the Faculty of the University;

(6)
“Dean” means the Dean of Faculty of the
University;

(7)
“Director” means  the head of a teaching Division

or an institute established as a constituent institute 
by the University;

(8)
“Head” means the Head of a teaching department
of the University;

(9)
“President” means the President of Al-Hamd
Educational Society;

(10)
“Patron” means the Patron of the University;

(11)
“Rector” means the Rector of the University;

(12)
“Registrar” means the Registrar of the University;

(13)
“Society” means Al-Hamd Educational Society

established under the Voluntary Social Welfare 
Agencies
 
(Registration
 
&
 
Control) 
Ordinance,1961 (XLVI of 1961).

(14)
“Rules and Regulations” means the respectively

the Rules and Regulations made or deemed to 
have been made under this Act;

(15)
“Teacher” means Professors, Associate Professors,

Assistant Professors and Lecturers engaged as a 
whole-time by the University for teaching courses 
of studies prescribed for graduation or post 
graduate classes and such other persons as may be 
declared to be Teachers by Regulations;

(16)
“Teaching Department” means a teaching

department maintained and administrated or 
recognized by; University;

(17)
“University” means Al-Hamd Islamic University;

Establishment and 
incorporation of the

3.
(1)
There shall be established, in accordance with the 
provisions of this Act, a University to be called the Al-Hamd

University.
Islamic University consist of.–

(a)
The Patron, Chancellor, the 
Rector, the 
Deans and the Board of Governors;

(b)
the members of such councils,
 
committees and other  bodies as 
the 
respective Boards may 
establish;

(c)
the teacher and student of the University 
and its constituent 
units; and

(d)
such other officers and members 
of 
the staff as may, from time to time,
 
be 
specified by the respective 
Board.

(2)
The University shall be a body corporate by the 
name of the Al-Hamd Islamic University having perpetual 
succession and a common seal, with power, among other, to 
acquire, hold and dispose of any property or investments and 
shall be the said name sue  and be sued.

(3)
The University shall have its principal seat at 
Quetta and may set up any number of campuses with the prior 
approval of Government at such places as the Board may 
determine.

4.
The University shall have the powers—

Powers and function 
of the University.

(a)
to provide for instruction in such branches of 
learning as it may deem fit, and to make provision 
for research and for the advancement and 
dissemination of knowledge in such manner as it 
may determine;

(b)
to admit and examine students;

(c)
to hold examinations and to award and confer 
degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other 
academic distinctions to and on persons who have 
been admitted to and have passed its 
examinations under prescribed conditions;

(e)
to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions

on persons as approved in the manner as may be 
prescribed;

(f)
to pursue research;

(h)
to decide teaching methods and strategies in order 
to ensure the most effective educational and 
training programmes;

(i)
to affiliate or associate, itself with other 
institutions for effective discharge of its functions 
and responsibilities;

(j)
to provide for the teaching  of specified courses 
and training for persons not being students of the 
University and grant certificates  and diplomas to 
such persons;

(k) 
to recognize the examination  passed or   the 
period of study spent at other university or places 
of learning as equivalent to examinations or 
periods of study in the university or to withdraw 
such recognition;

(l)
to
 
institute
 
professorships,
 
associate 
professorships, assistant professorships and 
lectureships and any other posts and to appoint 
persons thereto;

(n)
to create posts for research, publications, 
extension administration and other related 
purpose and to appoint person thereto;

(p)
to promote the extra curricular and recreational 
activities of such students and to make 
arrangements for promoting their health and
general welfare;

(q)
to establish teaching departments, institutes, 
museums, laboratories, workshops, hospitals, 
farms, and provide facilities to other center of 
excellence, and study centers for the development 
of teaching and research and to make such 
arrangements for their maintenance, management 
and administration as it may determine;

(r)
to enter into, carry out, vary or, cancel contracts;

(s)
to provide for the printing and publication of 
research and other works; and

(t)
to do all such other acts and things, whether 
incidental to the power of aforesaid or not, as may 
be requisite in order to further objective of 
university as a place of education, learning and 
research.

University open to 
all classes, creeds, 
etc.

5.
The University shall be open to all persons of either sex 
and whatever religion, race, creed, class or color, and domicile 
who are academically and morally qualified for admission to the 
courses of study offered by the University and no such person 
shall be denied the privileges of the University on the ground 
only of sex, creed, religion, race, class, color, or domicile.

Teaching and 
examinations.

6.
(1)
The academic programmes of the University shall 
be conducted in the prescribed manner.

(2)
The University shall restrict to phase-wise 
development of its academic programmes and having developed 
the necessary infrastructure it shall launch its academic 
programmes subsequently.

(3)
The University may associate external examiners 
for the conduct of examinations.

(4)
No degree shall be granted unless a student has 
passed an examination in Islamic and Pakistan studies at the 
Bachelor’s degree level or, in the case of a non-Muslim student, 
in Ethics and Pakistan Studies at his option.

7.
The following shall be the Authorities of the University:-

Authorities of the 
University.

(a)
the Academic Council;

(b)
the Advance studies and Research Board;

(c)
the Board;

(d)
the Board of Faculty / Board of Studies;

(e)
the Selection Board: and

(f)
such other Authorities as may be specified by 
regulations to be the Authority.

Officers of the 
University.

8.
The following shall be the officers of the University, 
namely;-

(a)
the Chancellor;

(b)
the Rector;

(c)
the Deans;

(d)
the Directors;

(e)
the Registrar;

(f)
the Treasurer;

(g)
the Controller Examination;

(h)
such other persons as may be specified by 
Regulations to be the officers.

Patron.
9.
(1)
The Governor of 2[Balochistan] shall be the 
Patron of the University.

(2)
The Patron or his nominee shall preside at the 
convocation of the University.

(3)
Every Proposal to confer an honorary degree shall 
be subject to confirmation by the Patron.

Visitation.
10.
(1)
The Patron may cause a visitation or inquiry to be 
made in respect of any matter connected with affairs of the 
institute and appoint any such person as he may deem fit for the 
purpose.

(2)
The Patron may, on receipt of a report, issue such

directions as he thinks fit and the Chancellor shall comply with 
such directions.

Chancellor.
11.
(1)
The President of society shall be the Chancellor 
of the University.

(2)
The Chancellor shall appoint a Rector.

(3)
The Chancellor shall have the power to assent to 
such rules and regulations as required to be submitted to him by 
the society or withhold assent or refer them back to the society 
for reconsideration.

(4)
In case   the Chancellor is satisfied that the 
proceedings of any Authority or order of any officer are not in 
accordance with the provisions of this Act, the rules or 
regulations, he may, after calling upon such Authority or officer 
to show cause as to why such proceedings or, as the case may 
be, order should not be annulled, by order in writing, annul such 
proceedings or orders.

Rector.
12.
(1)
Rector shall be an eminent scholar of repute who 
shall be appointed by the Chancellor.

(2)
The Rector shall be the chief academic and 
administrative officer of the University and shall be responsible 
for the implementation of the decisions of the Board and for the 
execution of the programmes of the University in accordance 
with the guidelines and policies formulated by the Board.

(3)
The Rector shall-

(a)
submit plans of work and budget estimates 
of the University for the consideration of 
the Board;

(b)
direct the activities connected with the 
execution of programmes for instruction, 
training, research, demonstration, services 
to community, etc;

(d)
re-appropriate funds within the approved 
budget and report it to the Board in the
next meeting;

(e)
appoint, with the approval of the 
Board, teachers, officers and members of 
the staff of the University and such other 
persons as may be necessary in 
accordance with policies and procedures 
approved by the Board so as to ensure the 
highest intellectual and moral qualities in 
the persons appointed;

(f)
submit to the Board, in accordance with 
the rules of procedure made by it, reports 
on the activities of the University and the 
execution of the plans of work;

(g)
create and fill temporary posts for a period 
not exceeding six months; and

(h)
undertake any work assigned by the 
Board.

Board of Governors.
13.
(1)
The general supervision and control of 
administrative, academic and financial affairs and the power to 
lay down the policies of the University shall vest in a Board of 
Governors consisting of the following members, namely:-

(b)
Rector;

(c)
Chairman Higher Education Commission 
or his nominee not below the rank of an 
officer pay scale 20;

(f)
Secretary,
 
Education
 
Department, 
Government of Balochistan;

(h)
one Retired Judge of the High Court;

(k)
four persons, prominent in the field of 
their specialization because of their 
experience and achievements, to be 
nominated by the Society;

(l)
Registrar of the University, who shall be 
the secretary.

(2)
A nominated member of the Board shall hold 
office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for re-
nomination on the expiry of his term.

(3)
The office of a nominated member of the Board 
shall become vacant if he resigns or fails to attend three 
consecutive meetings of the Board with sufficient case or leave 
of absence.

(4)
A causal vacancy in the office of a member of the 
Board shall be filled by a person nominated by the Authority 
which nominates the member whose vacancy is to be filled.

(5)
No Act or proceedings of the Board shall be 
invalid by reason only of the existence of a vacancy in or a 
defect in the constitution of the Board.

14.
(1)
The Board shall exercise the power and perform 
the following functions, namely.—

Powers and 
functions of the 
Board.

(a)
to hold, control and administer the 
property, funds, assets and resources of 
the University;

(b)
to transfer and accept transfer of movable 
or immovable property on behalf of the 
University;

(c)
to consider  and approve, on the advice of 
the Finance and planning Committee, the 
annual and revised budget estimates and to

lay down guidelines or rules of business 
dealing with financial matters;

(d) 
to approve, carryout, vary or cancel 
contracts on behalf of the University.

(e)
to initiate and approve schemes for 
achievement of the objectives of the 
University;

(f)
to determine the form, and regulate the 
custody and use of common seal of the 
University;

(g)
to create professional, research, 
administrative posts and such other posts 
as may be required to carry out for the 
purposes of the University, and to suspend 
or abolish such posts;

(h)
to take all such initiatives as it may 
consider necessary or desirable for the 
efficient and effective management and 
functioning of the University;

(i) 
to suspend, punish and remove from 
service, employees of the University in the 
manner as may be prescribed after due 
enquiry and defense;

(j)
to approve regulations on the 
recommendations of the appropriate 
bodies; and

(k)
to determine and administer all other 
matters concerning the University.

(2)
The Board may delegate any of its powers to the 
Rector subject to such conditions as it may deem fit to impose.

Meetings of the 
Board.

15.
(1)
The Board shall meet, at least twice in a year on 
such dates as may be fixed by the Chancellor.

(2)
Special meeting may be called at any time once in 
a year by and on the direction of the Chancellor or on a request 
by not less than five members of the Board to consider any
matter of urgent nature.

(3)
In the case of special meeting not less than ten 
clear days notice shall be given to the members of the Board and 
the agenda of the meeting shall be restricted to the matter for 
which the special meeting is called.

(4)
The quorum for a meeting of the Board shall be 
on half of its members, a fraction being counted as one.

(5)
The decision of the Board shall be expressed in 
terms of the views of the majority of the members present and 
voting and, if the members are equally divided, the Chairman of 
the Board shall have a casting vote.

Director.
16.
(1)
The Board may appoint a Director of each 
campus of the Institute, on such terms and conditions, as it may 
determine.

(2)
The Director of a campus shall have the 
following powers, namely:-

(b)
to sanction re-appropriation of an amount 
not exceeding such amount as the Board 
may authorise in this behalf for an 
unforeseen item not provided for in the 
budget;

(c)
to make such arrangement for the scrutiny 
of papers, markers and results as may be 
necessary ; and

(d) 
to direct teachers, officers and other 
employees of the campus of the Institute 
to take up such assignments in connection 
with teaching, research, examination, 
administration and such other activities in 
the campus, as he may consider necessary.

Academic Council.
17.
(1)
Academic Council shall consist of–

(a) 
the rector who shall be its Chairman;

(b) 
all Deans;

(c) 
the Directors of the respective campuses;

(d) 
the Heads of the Teaching Departments;

(e) 
the Controller Examination;

(f) 
all Professors of the University; and

(2)
Members appointed by nomination shall hold 
office for three years and shall be eligible for   re- nomination.

(3)
The quorum for a meeting of the Academic 
Council shall be one half of the total number of its members, a 
fraction being counted as one.

Powers of the 
Academic Council.

18.
(1)
The Academic Council shall be the academic 
body of the University and shall, subject to the provisions of this 
Act and the Statutes, have the powers to lay down proper 
standards of instructions, research, publications and 
examinations and to regulate and promote the academic standard 
of the University.

(2)
In particular and without prejudice to the 
generality  of the foregoing provisions, and the Statutes, the 
Academic Council shall have the powers-

(a) 
to advise the Board on academic matters;

(c) 
to regulate the admission of students to the 
courses of studies and examination in the 
University;

(e) 
to propose to the Board schemes for the 
constitution and organization of faculties 
and teaching departments;

(f) 
to consider or formulate proposals for the 
planning and development of teaching and 
research in the University;

(g)
to make regulations prescribing the 
courses of studies; the syllabi and the 
outlines of tests for all University 
examinations subject to the approval of 
the Board;

(h) 
to regulate the award of fellowships, 
scholarships,
 
stipends,
 
bursaries, 
exhibitions, medals and prizes;

(j) 
to appoint or nominate members to the 
various authorities in accordance with 
provisions of this Act; and

(k) 
to perform such other functions as may be 
prescribed by statutes.

Constitutions, 
functions and 
powers of 
authorities.

19.
Subject to the provisions of this Act, the constitution, 
functions and the powers of the authorities for which no specific 
provision has been made in this Act shall  be such as may be 
prescribed by Statutes.

Committees.
20.
The Board, the Academic Council and any other 
authorities may, from time to time, appoint such standing, 
special or advisory committees as they may deem fit and may 
appoint such persons on these committees who are not members 
of the authorities appointing the committees.

Indemnity.
21.
(1)
No suit, prosecution or legal proceedings shall lie 
against the University, Board, any Authority or an employee of 
the University for anything, which is done, or intended to be 
done in good faith under this Act.

(2)
No decision taken, or thing done, by the 
Chancellor or the Board shall be called in question before any 
court or other authority.

Power to make rules.
22.
(1)
Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Board 
may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

(2)
Without prejudice to the generality of the 
foregoing powers, such rules may provide for:—

(a)
terms and conditions of 
contractual 
appointments of 
teachers, 
researchers and 
officers;

(b)
powers and duties of officers and teachers;

(c)
conditions under which the University 
may enter into arrangements with other 
public or private organizations for 
purposes of instructions, research and 
other scholarly activities;

(f)
acquisition and administration of 
properties and investments in the fund of 
the University; and

(g)
all other matters which under this Act are 
required to be regulated by rules.

(3)
The Rector, the Director, the deans or the 
Academic Council may propose the draft of the rules of the 
Board.

(4)
Any Authority or body of the University may 
propose rules, consistent with the provisions of this Act, for 
approval of the Board, to regulate the conduct of its business.

Statutes.
23.
(1)
Subject to the provisions of this Act, Statutes may 
be made to regulate or prescribe all or any of the following 
matters, namely:-

(a)
creation of Faculties, Teaching 
Departments and other Academic Units 
and Divisions;

(b)
service, pension and fringe benefits for 
University employees and terms and 
conditions of their service;

(c)
efficiency and discipline of the University 
employees; and

(d)
all matters required to be regulated under 
the statues.

(2)
The Board shall propose draft of the Statutes for 
approval by the society which may approve them, or refer them 
back for reconsideration, and no statue shall be valid until the 
Society has approved it.

(3)
Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-
section (2), the Statutes set out in the Schedule to this Act shall 
be deemed to be the Statutes framed under this section and shall 
remain in force until they are rescinded or replaced by new 
Statues framed in accordance with this Act.

Removal of 
difficulties.

24.
(1)
If any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of 
the provisions of this Act, the Chancellor may make such order, 
not in consistent with the provision of this Act, as may appear to 
him to be necessary for removing the difficulty.

(2)
Where this Act makes any provision for anything 
to be done but no provision or no sufficient provision has been 
made as respect the authority of whom, or the time at which, or 
the manner in which, it should be done, then it shall be done by 
such authority, at such time, or in such manner as the Chancellor 
may direct.
THE SCHEDULE

Faculties.
1.
There shall be a faculty for a teaching department or a 
group of teaching departments. The University shall include the 
following faculties and such other faculties as may be prescribed 
by the Board.

(a)
Faculty of Islam.

(b)
Faculty of Science.

(c)
Faculty of Arts.

(d)
Faculty of Engineering; and

(e)
Such other Faculty as may by prescribed by the
statutes.

2.
(1)
There shall be a Board of each faculty which shall 
consist of-

Board of 
Faculty/Board of 
Studies.

(a)
the Dean;

(c)
one member other than Professors and 
Head of each teaching department to be

two teachers to be nominated by the 
Academic Council by reason of their 
specialized knowledge of the subjects 
which, though not assigned to the Faculty, 
have in the opinion of the Academic 
Council, important bearing on the subjects 
assigned to the Faculty;

(e)
two experts in the field from outside the 
University to be appointed by the Board; 
and

(f)
one member to be nominated by 
the 
Rector.

(2)
The members, other than ex-officio members,

(3)
The quorum for a meeting of the Board of a 
Faculty shall be one-half of the total number of members, a 
fraction being counted as one.

Functions of the 
Board of Faculty.

3.
The Board of each Faculty shall, subject to the general 
control of the Academic Council and the Board, have the powers 
to–

(a)
co-ordinate the teaching, and research 
work in the subjects assigned to the 
Faculty;

(b)
scrutinise the recommendations of the 
Board of Studies, comprising the Faculty 
with regard to the appointment of paper-

setters and examiner for graduate and post 
graduate examinations and to forward the 
panels of suitable paper-setters and 
examiners for each examination to the 
Rector;

(c)
consider any other academic matter 
relating to the faculty and report thereon 
to the Academic Council;

(d)
prepare a comprehensive annual report 
regarding the performance of each 
department, comprising the Faculty for 
presentation to the Academic Council; and

(e)
perform such other functions as may be 
prescribed by Statutes.

Dean
4.
(1)
There shall be a Dean of each Faculty who shall 
be the Chairperson and convener of the Board of Faculty.

(2)
The Dean shall be appointed by the Board on the 
recommendation of Rector from amongst the three most senior 
Professors or Associate Professor or any other person deem fit 
for the purpose and shall hold office for a period up to three 
years and shall be eligible for re-appointment.

(3)
The Dean shall present candidates for admission 
to degree (except honorary degrees) in the courses falling within 
the purview of the Faculty.

(4)
The Dean shall have such powers and duties as 
may be prescribed by the Board on the recommendations of the 
Rector.

Academic 
Departments and 
Head of 
Departments.

5.
(1)
There shall be an academic department for each 
subject or a group of subjects as may be prescribed by 
Regulations and a Head of department shall head each academic 
department.

(2)
The Head of an academic department shall be 
appointed by the Board on the recommendations of the Rector 
from amongst three senior most Professors or Associate 
Professor  other than Professor any other person deem fit for the 
purpose and shall hold office for a period up to three years and
shall be eligible for re-appointment:

Provided that in a department in which there is no 
Professor or Associate Professors, the appointment shall be 
made from amongst the three senior most Associate Professors 
and Assistant Professors of the department, beside it shall be 
look after by the Dean of the Faculty with the assistance of the 
senior most teacher of the department.

(3)
The Head of department shall plan, organize and 
supervise the work of the department and shall be responsible to 
the Dean for the work of his department.

(4)
The Head of department shall, under the general 
supervision of the Rector and the Dean, exercise all 
administrative, financial and academic powers and such other 
duties or powers as may be delegated to him.

(5)
The Head of department shall prepare a 
comprehensive annual report regarding the performance of 
department at the graduate and postgraduate levels, Faculty 
research and development and submit this report to the Dean of 
the Faculty for his evaluation.

(a)
the Rector who shall be its 
Chairperson;

Board of Advance 
Studies and

all the Deans;

one University professor from each

three members from the relevant field 
Research Organizations and government

The team of office of the members of the Board

(1)
The Selection Board shall consist of –

(a)
the Rector who shall be its Chairperson;

(b)
the Dean of the Faculty concerned;

(d)
one member of the Board to be nominated 
by the Board.

one eminent scientist or scholar to be

(f)
one expert in the subject to be nominated

The Registrar shall be the Secretary of the 
Selection Board.
